answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a separate bond before it can bridge into paid work, viewing trust through the prism of capital at risk. A fake profile can mirror an honest agent, but it cannot reuse that agent's bond. Funds remain locked through a dispute window and are slashed for cryptographically provable double billing. Creating 1,000 identities therefore requires 1,000 bonds, tying up capital and exposing it to loss when those identities cheat.
